subject: math

objective.text: Measure objects with a 12-inch ruler and a yardstick. Pick the unit and the tool that fit the object.

explanations.title: Inch, foot and yard
explanations.text: An inch is a small unit. A foot is 12 inches. A yard is 3 feet. A 12-inch ruler measures 1 foot.

explanations.title: Pick a unit that fits
explanations.text: Small things, like a pencil, fit inches. Longer things, like a rug, fit feet. Very long things, like a street, fit yards.

explanations.title: Pick a tool that fits
explanations.text: A 12-inch ruler is good for short objects. A yardstick is good for long objects. A long object needs fewer moves with a yardstick.

explanations.title: A yardstick is 3 feet
explanations.text: Every yardstick length is 3 feet. Lay a yardstick 2 times to measure 2 yardsticks. That is 3 feet plus 3 feet.

explanations.title: One yardstick, three units
explanations.text: You can measure in inches, feet or yards with a yardstick. Pick the unit that fits the object.

explanations.title: Compare to a yardstick
explanations.text: Before you measure, guess. Is the object more than, less than, or about the same length as the yardstick?

examples.title: Billy's pencil
examples.text: Billy says his pencil is 7 feet long. A foot is long, so this is too long. A pencil fits inches. He can say 7 inches.

examples.title: Yardstick laid 2 times
examples.text: A rug is 2 yardsticks long. Each yardstick is 3 feet. 3 plus 3 is 6. The rug is 6 feet long.

hints.text: Pick a unit that fits the object. Small things use small units.
Is the object longer than a ruler? A long object needs a tool with fewer moves.
Every yardstick length is 3 feet. Do not count each yardstick as 1 foot.
Think about how long a yardstick is. Is the object shorter or longer?

hints.text: Think about the 12-inch ruler and the yardstick. How do the units fit together?
Think about how big a foot is. Is a pencil that long?

Count by threes. Start at the first number.
Think of each number as tens and ones. Add the tens, then the ones.

visual_generation_rules: Diffusion cannot count reliably. Any picture where an exact number of objects matters must be built by code (SVG or widget) or drawn by an artist.

Every visual must be checked by a person: the count shown must equal the stimulus in the question and the rubric answer key.
Animations are described as frames with exact counts per frame, so they can be built or generated and then checked frame by frame.
